quads.note: Mixed 50/50 split. High reps introduce massive lung and systemic fatigue.

hamstrings.note: Fast-twitch. Highly explosive layout; high reps must stay light.

glutes.note: Strongest muscle group. High reps create massive cardiovascular demand.

adductors.note: Require smooth transitions; avoid jerky movements (groin risk).

abductors.note: Outer hip stabilizers. Best with high-rep lateral cable or band work.

calves.note: Gastrocnemius (diamond upper calf). Best with straight-leg raises.

soleus.note: Flat/deep lower calf. Incredibly high endurance; bent-knee work above 65%.

tibialis.note: Shin muscle. Hard to injure; keep constant tension for a high burn.

chest.note: Mixed-fiber pectoral; productive across the whole rep spectrum.

lats.note: Wide window; heavy pulls and high-rep pulldowns both work.

back.note: General mid-back window; rows cover it well.

traps.note: Responds to heavy shrugs plus long-duration holds.

shoulders_lateral.note: Side delts are slow-twitch; a too-light weight simply cruises.

rear_delts.note: Fast-twitch. Power collapses from set 1 to set 2; keep later sets honest.

biceps.note: Mixed fibers; strict curls across the window.

triceps.note: Fast-twitch. Drops drastically from set 1 to set 2 — respect the floor.

forearms.note: Endurance-rich; constant tension and high reps work best.

core.note: Abs are slow-twitch; too-light weight cruises without growth.

obliques.note: Avoid heavy low-reps to prevent widening the waistline.

erectors.note: Lumbar disc risk. Never train high-reps to absolute structural failure.

hip_flexors.note: High-rep controlled knee drives; low injury tolerance.

serratus.note: Scapular stabilizer; protraction with full reach.

neck.note: Spine isolation tax — prioritize impeccable static posture over load.

rhomboids.note: Endurance postural muscle; squeeze and hold.

infraspinatus.note: Rotator cuff — strict form with light bands or cables.

supraspinatus.note: Cuff — thumb-up raises only, never heavy.

brachialis.note: Elbow flexor; hammer and reverse curls.

brachioradialis.note: Forearm flexor; reverse curls and neutral grips.

anconeus.note: Tiny elbow stabilizer; light high-rep work.

pec_minor.note: Deep pec layer; protraction and depression.

popliteus.note: Knee unlocker — tiny controlled loads only.

peroneus_tertius.note: Ankle eversion; band work with slow tempo.

multifidus.note: Spinal stabilizer — never to structural failure.

transverse.note: Deep core; bracing quality over load.
